subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput follow-up & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of FinPay requirements (from call):
- Target p95 latency: <= 50ms for short-response requests (prompts ~256 tokens)
- Sustained throughput: ~150 req/s for normal hours; burst to 300 req/s for peak payment-window (~20-30 mins)
- SLA expectation: 99.95% uptime, predictable tail latency
- Data residency: US only (no cross-region routing)

What we recommend based on the above: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) — primarily because your p95 latency and burst throughput requirements are best served by capacity isolation and pinned model-serving instances. Benefits for FinPay:
- Predictable tail latency (no noisy neighbor effects)
- Configurable autoscaling and burst capacity for the payment window
- Data isolation to meet PCI-adjacent controls (when combined with private networking)

That said, a short hosted pilot could help validate prompt engineering and baseline costs. If you want to move fast and validate functionality, we can run a hosted pilot (small scale) while we onboard Dedicated capacity for production. 

Attachments: I ran the quick benchmark we discussed on our reference config; attaching the CSV with latency percentiles and throughput curves (finpay_latency_benchmarks.csv).

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm preference: Dedicated reserve vs hosted pilot (reply with preferred path)
2) If Dedicated: I’ll loop in Solutions (Marissa) to scope the reserve sizing + SOW draft (timeline: 2-3 business days)
3) If Hosted pilot: we’ll set up a trial API key and a short test plan (2 weeks)
4) Procurement: if you need a draft SOW/quote to start procurement, I can attach one.

Could you confirm which path you want to take and share any procurement timelines?

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
dylan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0173

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finpay.com>

Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput follow-up & next steps

Thanks Dylan — useful recap. A few quick clarifying questions before we lock in Dedicated: 

1) Cost delta: can you give a ballpark on committed monthly cost vs hosted pay-as-you-go for the baseline 150 req/s with the burst profile? Even ranges are fine.
2) Autoscale timing: for the 20-30 minute payment window burst, can Dedicated scale fast enough or do we need a pre-warmed burst pool?
3) SLA & support: is 99.95% SLA available on Dedicated right away or only as part of an enterprise package?
4) Procurement: our legal will want a draft SOW + security addendum for SOC 2 evidence.

Also quoting your note below for context: 
> That said, a short hosted pilot could help validate prompt engineering and baseline costs. If you want to move fast and validate functionality, we can run a hosted pilot (small scale) while we onboard Dedicated capacity for production.

Our preference would be to avoid double work — if Dedicated gives us the latency guarantees and autoscale behavior we need, we’d prefer to go straight to that. Procurement timeline: we have a purchase committee meeting on 2027-07-01 and would like a draft SOW by 2027-06-25 if possible.

—Alex
Alex Turner
VP of Engineering | FinPay
alex.turner@finpay.com | +1 (212) 555-0124
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated: latency/throughput follow-up & next steps

Alex — great, thanks for the clear timeline. Answering your questions and next steps below: 

1) Cost delta (ballpark):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): lower upfront; for your baseline ~150 req/s and expected token mix, estimate ~$25-35k/month variable depending on usage patterns.
- Dedicated (reserved): higher committed monthly (roughly $45-60k/month for the reserve we expect you'll need) but predictable unit cost and significantly lower per-token serving cost at scale. Exact numbers depend on model selection and quantization profile; I’ll include both options in the SOW.

2) Autoscale / burst: Dedicated supports a pre-warmed burst pool and sub-10s scale-to-warm transitions if configured. For 20-30 minute payment windows we recommend a small pre-warmed burst allocation to guarantee tail latency — we’ll size that in the SOW and you can tune after the first week of traffic.

3) SLA & support: 99.95% SLA is available on Dedicated when paired with our enterprise support tier and an agreed SLO in the contract. For procurement we can include the SLA language and support tier options in the SOW.

4) Procurement items: attached draft SOW (FP_SOW_draft_v1.docx) and I’ll loop in Security for the SOC 2 evidence pack. Marissa — can you own the SOW iteration and security artifact bundle for FinPay? Neha — please confirm estimated onboarding start date if we get procurement complete by 2027-07-05.

Proposed immediate actions:
- I’ll upload a full draft SOW + pricing worksheet to the Drive and share the link (linked above).
- Marissa to own SOW edits and technical scoping.
- Set a 30-minute alignment call next week (I’ll add a scheduling poll).

If that timeline works for you, we’ll mark this as Dedicated-forward and deliver the SOW by 2027-06-25 to hit your procurement window.

Thanks — talk soon.
Dylan

--

Account Executive | Redwood Inference
